equations.fully_centred_textbook: A_c(K, y) = <H K H, H T H>_F / (||H K H||_F ||H T H||_F),  T = y y^T,  y in {-1,+1}^n,  H = I_n - (1/n) 1 1^T
equations.implemented_train_objective: A_impl(K, y) = <H K H, y y^T>_F / (||H K H||_F ||y y^T||_F)   (target uncentred; src/qkv2x/quantum/train.py L22-34)
equations.identity: A_impl = 4 pi (1 - pi) * A_c  with pi = positive fraction (numerators identical since H is idempotent; ||y y^T||_F = n while ||H T H||_F = 4 n pi (1 - pi)); every optimisation batch has pi = 1/2 exactly, where 4 pi (1 - pi) = 1, so A_impl == A_c on all batches

batch_protocol.how_minibatches_are_formed: src/qkv2x/quantum/train.py::_balanced_batch: draw batch//2 = 256 indices uniformly from the positive class and 256 from the negative class (numpy default_rng, without replacement whenever the class pool >= 256, which holds for every production label vector audited here), concatenate and shuffle. One such batch is drawn per epoch (200 epochs).
batch_protocol.labels_are_pm1: yes: train.py L90 maps y -> ypm = where(y > 0, +1.0, -1.0) before the target Gram T = outer(ypm, ypm) is formed
batch_protocol.batches_exactly_balanced: yes: pi = 1/2 exactly in every batch by construction; empirically confirmed on 4000/4000 audited draws (2 real label vectors x 2 rngs x 1000 draws), all exactly 256+256
batch_protocol.alignment_averaged_across_batches: no: the objective each epoch is the centred KTA of that single balanced batch (train.py L98-110); history records the per-batch value and the retained parameters are those of the best SINGLE batch (max over epochs, train.py L112-116). No cross-batch averaging anywhere.
batch_protocol.same_code_path_in_checkpointed_runs: veremi_nextgen_exp.py::_qtrain_checkpointed L456-457 imports and uses the same _balanced_batch/_centered_kta_torch

dev_grid_s7.split: group_split(test_frac=0.3, val_frac=0.15, seed=7) then _cap_train_groupwise(max_train=3000, seed=7) -- the exact scripts/dev_multiseed.py recipe that built the cached Gram

nextgen.split: official NextGen split field == "Train" (veremi_nextgen_exp.py L368 index rule; stored row order)

gram_provenance.dev_grid_s7_crosslayer: results/dev_grid_multiseed/checkpoints/gram_qsvm_crosslayer_s7.npz::K_tr (trained cross-layer map, seed 7, built by scripts/dev_multiseed.py)
gram_provenance.nextgen_binary_full_crosslayer: results/veremi_nextgen/checkpoints/gram_binary_full_qsvm_crosslayer.npz::K_tr (trained cross-layer map, official NextGen Train rows, built by src/qkv2x/experiments/veremi_nextgen_exp.py)

protocol.textbook_alignment: independent numpy H K H / H T H implementation (+1e-12 denominator guard, matching train.py)

headline: The implemented objective centres K but not T; this is EXACTLY equivalent to the fully centred textbook alignment on every optimisation batch because batches are exactly class-balanced by construction. Batch protocol: _balanced_batch draws 256 positives + 256 negatives (batch = 512, configs/quantum.yaml::train.batch) each epoch; labels are exactly {-1,+1}; alignment is per-batch, NOT averaged across batches (best single-batch parameters retained). Audit: 4000/4000 draws from the two real trained-run label vectors (dev_grid s7 pi=0.2259, NextGen Train pi=0.2240) were exactly 256+256. On the real cached cross-layer Grams, implemented vs fully centred agree to max|diff| = 5.66e-15 over 400 balanced subsets (machine precision), while over 400 imbalanced subsets (pi in [0.10, 0.90]) the discrepancy follows A_impl = 4pi(1-pi)*A_c with max identity error 1.09e-14 and ratio-vs-factor fit slope 1.000000/1.000000, R^2 1.000000/1.000000 (dev_grid/nextgen).
